title: Story of the Second Lunatic (Português)

full_text:
Moving through the corridors of the hospital, Sultan Mohammed encountered a second inmate sitting upon a stone bench, holding a dry twig and drawing geometric circles in the sand.

'Peace be upon thee, friend,' said the Sultan. 'What kingdom art thou measuring in the sand?'

The inmate looked up with eyes sparkling with unburdened joy:
'I am measuring the kingdom of complete tranquility, which has no walls, no guards, and no rivals.

Before they brought me here, I was a wealthy merchant owning seven ships in the Red Sea. Every night I tossed in bed, tormented by anxieties: Will the monsoon sink my spices? Will pirates raid my silk? Will the harbor master double his bribes? Will my competitors ruin my prices? I had bags of gold, yet I could not eat bread without stomach spasms or sleep two hours without nightmares.

Then one storm wrecked five ships, and fire consumed my warehouses. I lost everything.
When I sat on the beach with nothing left but my wool tunic, a sudden miraculous breeze touched my face. For the first time in thirty years, I took a deep breath without fear! I realized I had nothing left to lose!

I sang with joy, gave away my remaining shoes, and began contemplating the stars. My relatives, seeing me dancing without money, concluded I had lost my wits and sent me here.
Yet look at me now: I eat fresh lentil porridge, drink pure well water, sleep like an innocent child, and have no fear of thieves, storms, or kings.
Tell me, sovereign visitor: who has the greater kingdom—he who trembles over gold, or he who rejoices in an empty hand?'

The Sultan sighed with profound humility, recognizing that true liberation is not the accumulation of possessions, but freedom from the fear of losing them.
moral: Freedom from material desire brings tranquility that kings and conquerors can never purchase. [PT]
